36 The electromotive force (e.m.f.) of a cell is 6.0 V. It has negligible internal resistance and is
connected across a resistor. The potential difference (p.d.) across the resistor is also 6.0 V.
The e.m.f. and the p.d. have the same numerical value but represent different processes.
Which statement about the different processes is correct?
A
The e.m.f. is the energy transferred from chemical energy to electrical energy in the cell and
the p.d. is the energy transferred from electrical energy to thermal energy in the resistor.
B
The p.d. is the energy transferred from chemical energy to electrical energy in the cell and
the e.m.f. is the energy transferred from electrical energy to thermal energy in the resistor.
C
The e.m.f. is the energy transferred per unit charge from chemical energy to electrical energy
in the cell and the p.d. is the energy transferred per unit charge from electrical energy to
thermal energy in the resistor.
D
The p.d. is the energy transferred per unit charge from chemical energy to electrical energy
in the cell and the e.m.f. is the energy transferred per unit charge from electrical energy to
thermal energy in the resistor.

hints: Notice the question labels $6.0\text{ V}$ as e.m.f. in the cell and $6.0\text{ V}$ as p.d. across the resistor, so track where charge gains and loses energy.
Recall that $1\text{ V} = 1\text{ J C}^{-1}$, so both e.m.f. and p.d. must be described as energy transferred per unit charge, not total energy.
Link the direction of transfer to the component: chemical to electrical in the cell for e.m.f., electrical to thermal in the resistor for p.d.
walkthrough: Identify the setup: a $6.0\text{ V}$ cell of negligible internal resistance connected only to a resistor, so charge gains energy in the cell and loses the same amount per coulomb in the resistor.
State the definitions: e.m.f. $E = W/Q$ is work done on charge per unit charge by the source, and p.d. $V = W/Q$ is work done by charge per unit charge in the load.
Check units: $\text{V}$ means $\text{J C}^{-1}$, so any statement calling e.m.f. or p.d. simply the energy transferred is incomplete.
Assign the correct energy conversion: in the cell chemical energy becomes electrical potential energy of charge, in the resistor electrical energy becomes thermal energy.
Combine both points: only the statement with per unit charge and chemical to electrical for e.m.f. plus electrical to thermal for p.d. is fully correct. This is option C.

A.explanation: Correct energy changes are identified but $6.0\text{ V}$ is not total energy, it is energy per unit charge in $\text{J C}^{-1}$.

B.explanation: The processes are swapped and the per unit charge part is missing: p.d. does not create electrical energy in the cell.

C.explanation: E.m.f. is work done on charge in the cell and p.d. is work done by charge in the resistor, both measured as energy per unit charge.

D.explanation: Includes per unit charge but swaps the locations: e.m.f. belongs to the cell and p.d. belongs to the resistor.
